lines.text: Do you know how your phone takes bright photos in the dark? It doesn't take one photo. It takes a burst.
In dim light, each pixel catches only a few particles of light. Too few, so the picture fills with random grain, called noise.
Keeping the shutter open longer collects more light. But your hand shakes, and everything blurs.
So night mode grabs many short shots instead, sometimes more than a dozen in a few seconds.
Software lines them all up, shifting each frame to cancel out the shake.
Then it averages them. Real detail is the same in every frame, so it stays. Noise is random, so it cancels out. Sixteen frames cut the noise by four.
Finally, it lifts the shadows, tames the bright lights, and fixes the colours.
So one night photo is really a stack of dark ones, added together.
